title: Multicenter international prospective study, sample size planned, to examine unilateral pectineal suspension (UPS)
summary:
The aim is to provide scientific evidence that the mesh-free unilateral pectineal suspension (UPS) ensures successful correction of genital prolapse. Our own retrospective data support the hypothesis that UPS leads to successful and lasting correction of apical descent with a high rate of patient acceptance (17,18). Now, the success of descent correction using UPS is to be prospectively investigated and compared with our own data on the robotic pectopexy we have published (13) as well as with published data on established standard procedures (15,19). The success of surgical descent correction will be measured using a defined composite endpoint (1) that includes both subjective and objective endpoints (primary study objective). 
Secondary study objectives: To collect data on patient satisfaction before and after surgery, standardized questionnaires will be used. The questionnaires will be administered before surgery and during follow-up visits 3–6 and 12–15 months after surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Isolated or combined apical descent, Grade 2 to Grade 4
Indication for apical prolapse correction
Patient requests surgical correction
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient language skills, making it impossible to complete the questionnaires
Severe physical or mental illnesses
Inability to give informed consent
Contraindications to the planned surgical procedure
